intro: A plate of mamak nasi lemak with fried egg is roughly 550 kcal. Most of the calories come from the coconut rice and the sweet, oily sambal.
diet: Yes, you don't need to cut nasi lemak out of your life. A regular plate with egg can still fit into your daily budget. What makes the calories jump is extra sides like ayam goreng or rendang. Stick to a regular portion and go easy on the add-ons.
tips: Swap the fried egg for a boiled egg to save some oil.
Ask for less sambal and extra cucumber.
If you want more protein, pick ayam bakar or a small ayam rempah, not a big piece of ayam goreng.

swap.name: Nasi lemak with boiled egg, less sambal
swap.why: You still get the nasi lemak taste, but with less oil from the fried egg and sambal.

faq.q: Why does mamak nasi lemak taste different from Malay stall nasi lemak?
faq.a: Every shop has its own sambal recipe and way of cooking the coconut rice. Mamak nasi lemak usually has a sweeter sambal and is sometimes eaten with curry.

faq.q: Is nasi lemak a good breakfast?
faq.a: Many Malaysians eat nasi lemak in the morning and it can keep you full until lunch. Make sure there's protein like egg so you stay full longer.

faq.q: Can I make a lighter nasi lemak at home?
faq.a: Yes. Use light coconut milk, or half coconut milk and half water. You can also cook the sambal with less oil and sugar.
